name: Dropbox
description: File storage and sharing service whose developer platform authorizes API access through OAuth 2.0 apps registered in its App Console.
notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Candidate families were enumerated from the Dropbox API documentation pages docs.dropboxapi.com (OAuth guide, Authorization, Authentication Types, Webhooks, Sharing; sources docs-dropboxapi-com-aea155a830, -2835da9ecb, -ee9def1cd1, -66542bc3bd, -68ce992b0c) read raw on 2026-10-04; the list is what those pages name, not a complete inventory. Deliberately not candidates: the app key (client_id), an identifier carried in authorization URLs; the OAuth authorization code and PKCE code verifier, which are transient exchange values; the OIDC id_token; and shared links, which the Sharing page describes as publicly accessible links with optional expiry, password or team-only visibility, not as credentials issued to an app. Whether any of these deserves a family is left to a maintainer.
